summary.text: Thomas Keane said technology has transformed clinical care and that AI is a major part of that transformation, including current uses such as note-taking for doctors and managing administrative tasks. In March 2026 Senate testimony, he said the administration believes in AI’s power to improve health care and is leading with a “try-first” culture, and in a June 2026 event he said HHS’s approach to the heterogeneous field must be nuanced. He described HHS/ONC efforts including a December 2025 RFI on accelerating AI use in clinical care and a proposed rule to streamline certification criteria and recenter the program on standards-based APIs and AI-enabled interoperability. He highlighted potential AI benefits such as flagging early signs of heart disease for rural clinicians without specialists and making health care more affordable, accessible, and supportive of improved outcomes.
